articles.summary: The Big Ten has the most wide-open race to make its conference championship game among the power five leagues.
articles.body:
The Big Ten has the most wide-open race to make its conference championship game among the power five leagues.

Four teams are still alive in the race to make it to Indianapolis next week. Three of those programs play in Top 25 rivalry battles in Week 13.

The UCLA Bruins and Oregon Ducks have win-and-in situations this weekend, but both of them are far from guarantees to win, especially the Bruins with their quarterback injuries.

The Iowa Hawkeyes need to win and get some help to book their ticket in the Big Ten Championship Game.

Due to the spread out nature of rivalry week, Iowa plays Friday afternoon and then might have to wait for Oregon's result in primetime on Saturday to learn their fate.

All of the weather forecasts for Week 13's biggest games can be found here on The Weather Channel.

Week 13 Top 25 Schedule, Odds and Weather

Mississippi State at No. 22 Ole Miss (-18.5)

Prediction: Ole Miss 34, Mississippi State 10

Forecast: Increasing Clouds, High of 56°F

Prediction: Florida 31, Florida State 28

Forecast: Chance of Showers, High of 48°F

No. 17 Oklahoma at No. 23 Missouri (-1.5)

No. 24 Washington at No. 12 Oregon (-14.5)

Prediction: Arizona 27, Arizona State 23

The simplest way for the Iowa Hawkeyes to reach the Big Ten Championship Game is to beat the Nebraska Cornhuskers on Friday and then have the USC Trojans beat the UCLA Bruins on Saturday.

That would allow Iowa to advance alongside Oregon thanks to the common opponents tiebreaker.

Iowa comes into its regular-season finale on a four-game winning streak in which its held opponents to 34 total points.

Kirk Ferentz's team is playing its best when it matters most, and it's gotten it to the edge of the College Football Playoff.

Nebraska stunned the Ohio State Buckeyes at home last week. It feels like the Huskers reside in a perfect letdown spot. It also doesn't help that they are 2-2 on the road with losses to Oregon and the Illinois Fighting Illini.

History isn't on the Huskers' side either, as they are 1-10 in their last 11 meetings with Iowa.

With all that in mind, it feels like a steal to get Iowa as a 4.5-point favorite at home.

The Hawkeyes defense is in great form and Nebraska sits in prime position for an emotional letdown after a rare Top 25 win.

UCLA resides in the most peril of the four Big Ten Championship Game contenders.

The Bruins are down to third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava, who struggled immensely in relief duty in overtime in last week's defeat to the Michigan Wolverines.

The good news for the Bruins is that USC's rushing defense gives up 124.5 yards per game. The Bruins may have to control the game with a rushing attack that averages 194 yards per contest.

Of course, the Trojans will lock in on the run and force Iamaleava to beat them through the air, which takes away UCLA's strength.

USC's defense as a whole is prone to conceding points. The Fresno State Bulldogs and Ohio State in Luke Fahey's first start in place of Julian Sayin were the only two teams not to score at least 20 points against the Trojans.

USC isn't a surefire lock to win. After all, this is college football and bizarre things happen every week.

The Trojans can score through Jayden Maiava and the aerial attack, and if they put up points early, the pressure will be on UCLA to keep up with its third-string quarterback.

UCLA would love to drag USC in a low-scoring, slow-paced game. That seems like the best way for the Bruins to win. No opponent scored more than 20 points on UCLA's defense since September 19.

Expert CFB Locks, Predictions for Week 13

Oregon simply needs to win to get into the Big Ten Championship Game.

Other scenarios may be in play by the time the Ducks kick off against Washington, but no matter what happens elsewhere, they just have to come out on top.

Dylan Raiola has led the Ducks to over 30 points in each of the last four games. The backup quarterback had at least 230 passing yards in every contest of that stretch.

It's easy to think Oregon will run right through the Washington defense and into the Big Ten Championship Game.

That very well could happen against a Washington team that's been through a taxing run dating back to Halloween. The Huskies had two road trips to the central time zone to play Nebraska and the Michigan State Spartans. They lost a tight game to the Penn State Nittany Lions and then beat Indiana at home in overtime.

Like Nebraska, Washington sits in an ideal let down spot on the road after its upset of Indiana.

Unlike Nebraska, the Huskies are a double-digit underdog in a rivalry that's been decided by 12 points or less in eight of the last nine meetings.

Oregon should win, but its defense has allowed 19.4 points per game and its been susceptible to some decent-sized concessions, including 28 to Ohio State and 26 to the Northwestern Wildcats.

Washington should be able to score a few times to keep itself within the number, but Oregon should win the game and advance to the Big Ten Championship Game.

articles.title: Expert CFB Locks, Predictions for Michigan vs. Ohio State and Week 13 Biggest Games
articles.summary: Just like that, we've reached our last full slate of games.
articles.body:
Just like that, we've reached our last full slate of games.

If we're being honest, it's hard to process. The season starts, it moves by in the blink of an eye and then the College Football Playoff arrives.

Rather than worry about the bracket or the Heisman, however, we're going to instead focus on this glorious lineup of games, many of which feature rivals, and celebrate the end of the regular season in style.

Have no fear; our picks aren't going anywhere. We'll have thoughts and picks for conference championship week, the bowl season, every single round of the College Football Playoff and the national championship.

There is still much to do, although there is no need to rush. Here is what we like in Week 13.

It's a sad football game. There's no getting around it.

It's a little less sad after Michigan found a way to beat unbeaten UCLA on Saturday, even if that football game was a tough watch, to say the least.

The Michigan offense was once again pretty powerless. UCLA had to play key moments with its third-string QB. The game ended thanks to college football's absurd overtime rules.

The Buckeyes, meanwhile, are officially removed from postseason consideration after a (slightly less) ugly loss to Nebraska. The team battled to stay in the game, although it wasn't enough.

Ryan Day has certainly had his struggles against Michigan in the past. He's currently 2-4 against his rival. Still, for as many issues as Ohio State has, Michigan has more of them.

The fact that this game is being played in Columbus is a tipping point.

It won't be fun to watch, although this rivalry is worth your time no matter the stakes. The Buckeyes win ugly.

Style points matter. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise. Oregon, which is vying for a playoff spot, knows this very well.

It's why the Ducks were still throwing the ball up 31 points against Michigan State last week. Dan Lanning wants to leave no doubt in the selection committee's mind, which brings us to this week.

Washington, meanwhile, just had its best moment of the season. The Huskies beat Indiana, the defending national champions, in thrilling fashion in overtime. With that, Washington has won four of its past five games.

Unlike Oregon, the Huskies don't have any chance at the playoff. Playing on the road after an emotional win against a team desperate to make an impression creates a fascinating situation, especially considering the game will be played in Eugene.

Oregon doesn't just win. It scores early and often because it has to.

On the topic of style points, enter BYU.

The Cougars barely kept their playoff hopes intact, surviving an overtime game against Kansas. It wasn't pretty, although they found a way. Despite that close call, the oddsmakers seem pretty bullish on the team's chances this weekend.

Cincinnati has already shown it can compete—and even beat—the best teams in the conference.

The Bearcats beat Texas Tech in the middle of the season in a convincing win. Since that game, however, Cincinnati is 1-4. The team's performance on the road is particularly worrisome. When traveling, the Bearcats are 0-4 and 1-3 against the spread.

BYU, squarely in the playoff mix, needs to win and also leave no doubt with the selection committee.

As such, expect a much cleaner performance, especially when playing at home. Expect this scoreboard to be lopsided from the start.

Although the Buffaloes have just four wins, the oddsmakers haven't given up just yet.

Colorado has clearly improved as the season progressed, albeit with a few clunkers along the way. Quarterback Isaac Wilson has given this team a spark, even if the turnovers have been an issue.

That was the case for Wilson last week against Cincinnati, as the QB threw three interceptions. Colorado added another fumble and still almost beat Cincinnati despite the miscues.

UCF hasn't exactly been sharp on the road, losing three of its four away games this year. Last week, however, the Knights were excellent, beating Iowa State 48-17 at home.

Despite that outcome, the Knights still feel like small underdogs on the road. Although teams will look at these teams' records and blissfully take the team with the winning record, we're going the other way.

We haven't always loved what Deion Sanders has done, but we like the way things are trending…for now.

Given the swirling conversation surrounding both coaches, this installment of South Carolina-Clemson is absolutely fascinating.

Dabo Swinney and Shane Beamer are fighting off the dreaded hot-seat conversation. While Swinney is likely to get more time to turn things around, Beamer could badly use this game.

The Clemson defense was excellent in last week's game against Duke, limiting the Blue Devils to less than 250 yards of offense. The offense wasn't dazzling, although it was good enough.

As for South Carolina, they played a competitive football game against Georgia. Well, at least in the first half. The Gamecocks trailed the Bulldogs 10-6 after 30 minutes, thanks in part to a spirited effort from its defense.

From there, Georgia took over. While South Carolina's offense couldn't muster much, the Bulldogs are on another level.

This week, going up against a quality defense, South Carolina does enough. In a close, low-scoring game, look for Beamer to ease concerns surrounding his job at the most critical time.

One team is 0-11. The other is 1-10. We like Northern Illinois, winless thus far, to finally end the streak this week. Over the past month, the Huskies have been far more competitive. Those efforts will be rewarded this week at home.

Style points. There are those words again. Indiana needs plenty of them to keep its playoff hopes intact. Blowing out Purdue is a necessity. While the offense has issues, Curt Cignetti finds a way for at least one week. Indiana by a ton.

Don't sleep on this sneaky-good game. While UTSA has played its way back into consideration for the College Football Playoff courtesy of the Group of Six path, Tulsa can play spoiler. Playing its best football of the year, the Golden Hurricanes find a way.

articles.standfirst: Semana clave con partidos de diferente calado ante Málaga, Numancia y Real Madrid
articles.summary: Semana clave con partidos de diferente calado ante Málaga, Numancia y Real Madrid
articles.body: El Athletic empieza sus exámenes de media temporada con una exigente semana de competición. En siete días los leones afrontarán dos partidos de Liga (Málaga y Real Madrid) y la segunda eliminatoria de Copa (Numancia) en lo que se anuncia como el primer gran test de Terzic. El equipo necesita un estímulo y estos tres partidos aparecen cargados de obligaciones. El conjunto rojiblanco viene de una triste derrota ante el Espanyol en un partido de escasa propuesta futbolística que provocó pitos en San Mamés. Los aficionados están recelosos respecto a las expectativas creadas con el fichaje del alemán. Pasadas 12 jornadas -todavía tienen pendiente el partido ante el Rayo- los leones corren el riesgo de caer en el desafecto: ahora mismo tienen Europa a tres puntos y el descenso a cuatro. Su balance en Liga es de cuatro victorias, cuatro empates y cuatro derrotas. La realidad del Athletic bien la firmaría el Málaga, su próximo rival, pero la necesidad de los blanquiazules se ha convertido en grave amenaza para el Athletic. El Málaga no ha ganado a nadie en su regreso a Primera División y es seguro que el primer derrotado tendrá mayor resonancia que en cualquier otra derrota. Así que en La Rosaleda el Athletic jugará sin fallo posible. El escenario quedará marcado por lo que ocurra en Málaga, aunque la sensación de partido definitivo la guardará siempre el enfrentamiento copero con el Numancia, rival ahora de menor categoría con el que se cruzará en Copa. Y ahí las obligaciones son eternas. El pantone de emociones se cerrará el domingo 6 de diciembre frente al Real Madrid en San Mamés. El duelo con los de Mourinho queda todavía a una distancia sideral tanto del pensamiento del vestuario como de las interrogantes de los aficionados por la importancia inmediata de los dos encuentros previos.

articles.title: Leny Yoro red card: Written reasons why Manchester United defender's red card at Liverpool was overturned published by the FA
articles.summary: Leny Yoro had a red card overturned after being sent off in Man Utd's 4-0 loss to Liverpool; Pro Ref chief Howard Webb agreed with the decision, but the FA ruled out the one-game suspension after Man Utd appeals; United used Pascal Strujk's red card for Brighton as part of their evidence
articles.body:
Yoro was sent off for bringing down Liverpool striker Alexander Isak as the last defender outside the penalty area, with referee Sam Barrott sending him off for a denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity (DOGSO), with VAR John Brooks agreeing with the call.

United went on to concede four goals in the heavy defeat to Liverpool - and despite Pro Ref chief Howard Webb indicating that no clear mistake was made, the FA still decided to overturn the red card for an "obvious error" by the officials, as Isak was not in possession of the ball when he was fouled.

In the written reasons, the three-person panel - consisting of three former professional footballers, including one goalkeeper - said Isak had taken a heavy touch "to the extent he had in fact lost control of the ball" - which under the rules, says Yoro should not have been sent off.

"The Commission members were unanimous that, taking the foul committed by Yoro out of the scenario, Isak would not have had an obvious goal-scoring opportunity," the statement read.

"Despite the fact that Isak had reached the ball initially, his touch was heavy to the extent that he had in fact lost control of the ball - that control had, in effect, passed to the advancing MUFC goalkeeper who in the view of the Commission would have been able to gather or smother the ball before AI [Alexander Isak] could get to it and shoot at goal.

"To the mind of the Commission, the referee had made an 'obvious error' in deciding that AI would have had an obvious goal-scoring opportunity."

The written reasons also said United provided extensive 'evidence' to say why Yoro should not have been sent off. As well as providing three separate angles of the incident, they also provided clips of Pascal Struijk's red card for Brighton against Sunderland - which was later overturned.

United's analysis also claimed that Isak was, "at best 1.8m short of reaching the ball". The FA said there was no way of determining that analysis themselves, so it was "viewed with caution and allocated weight accordingly".

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'D Up , Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Webb backed the process of his officials although was non-committal when sharing his own verdict on the incident.

"By and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," said Webb.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

Audio from the officials revealed the VAR Brooks, who backed referee Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.

This is not the first time this season that a DOGSO red card has created division within the football authorities.

In October, two independent panels disagreed over whether Brighton's Struijk deserved to be sent off at Sunderland, an event which United used in their evidence to get Yoro's red card overturned.

Struijk was dismissed for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity in the second half when he was adjudged to have fouled Sunderland striker Wilson Isidor as he tried to latch on to a pass that ran through to goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Neither referee Thomas Bramall nor his assistant gave a foul, but VAR Neil Davies intervened and recommended an on-field review. Bramall watched several replays before changing his decision and dismissing Struijk.

However, Brighton appealed and an independent regulatory commission, which is convened through the FA to consider disciplinary matters, overturned the red card and subsequent one-match ban.

But disagreements over the decision continued after the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel - another independent panel who determine the validity of refereeing decisions - voted 3-2 that the VAR intervention was correct.

The KMI panel ruled that Struijk committed a "cynical foul clearly impacting the attacker's ability to gain possession of the ball which should have been penalised by the referee".

articles.title: Man Utd's controversial refereeing decisions: Are officials making Mauricio Pochettino's job harder?
articles.summary: Man Utd have been plagued by refereeing decisions in Mauricio Pochettino's first two matches in charge against Liverpool and Sporting; United also received an apology from Pro Ref earlier this season for VAR's incorrect call in their defeat to Man City; But Utd's problems
articles.body:
Pochettino's first two games in charge have been plagued by controversial moments, following a similar pattern during the club's dreadful start, which has left them 19th, inside the Premier League relegation zone and out of the Carabao Cup.

United's luck appeared to be changing when Bruno Fernandes' shot was deflected in off a divot against Sporting on Wednesday, but the officials in Lisbon left Pochettino furious again as Amad Diallo's equaliser late in the first half was harshly ruled out for Youri Tielemans' foul in the build-up.

"It's difficult to answer as everyone saw it was impossible [to award a foul]," said Pochettino. "It's difficult to understand why that happened on the field."

Szymon Marciniak, referee in the 2022 World Cup final, had also already blown his whistle before Amad scored despite the forward being through on goal. Tielemans was booked for the tackle and the midfielder was later sent off after receiving a second yellow.

There was more controversy when United's third goal, and what they thought could be the winner, was ruled out following a VAR check. Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched the ball into his own net at a corner, although it was disallowed for Patrick Dorgu's foul.

Pochettino had already been complaining about officials this week with Leny Yoro's one-match suspension overturned on Tuesday after the defender was shown a straight red card with the score at 0-0 in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Yoro was dismissed for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity, although it appeared striker Alexander Isak wouldn't have reached the ball had the defender not fouled him.

Refereeing chief Howard Webb still backed the officials' process on Match Officials Mic'd Up , although he was non-committal when sharing his own verdict on the incident.

Pochettino also felt Liverpool's opening goal, scored by Dominik Szoboszlai from the free-kick conceded by Yoro, should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola was standing next to the Man Utd wall when the ball was struck.

Barcola appeared to be pushed towards the United defenders by Bruno Fernandes, revealing a grey area in the laws of the game, as they do not explain that type of incident.

The most significant incident of United's season came prior to Pochettino's arrival when United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner in Manchester City's 1-0 win in September which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu, but Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland, and Webb acknowledged the error.

In the same game, Man Utd benefited from Man City's Phil Foden being sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, a decision only narrowly backed 3-2 by the Key Match Incidents panel, while the United captain wrongly avoided a yellow card despite initiating the incident.

Yoro's red card against Liverpool wasn't the first time he has been harshly sent off for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity this season.

The defender was shown a straight red card when United trailed 1-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last month and then lost 2-0.

Yoro brought down Atletico's Jonathan David, who was heading away from goal, after the pair came together just inside United's half. "It is soft! No way, that should not be a red," said Sky Sports' Clinton Morrison.

articles.title: FIFA says personal and business information stolen in cyberattack
articles.summary: No files from the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed, according to media reports.
articles.body:
FIFA said it had been the victim of a criminal cyberattack that gave unauthorised access to personal and business information, although no files from the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed, according to media reports.

FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Al Jazeera.

FIFA strongly condemned the “unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data,” adding that such actions were “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”.

It also said that :”FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.”

FIFA did not say how many people or organisations were affected, when the attack took place or what the business information included. Its reference to publication did not say whether any data had appeared online, or where.

Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were FIFA files. Three days later, it appeared to take credit for the hack when responding to a post that said more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.

The person with knowledge of the matter told the Reuters news agency that less than 0.1 percent of the total data held by world football’s governing body was affected.

A FIFA source told The Athletic that the person – or group – responsible for carrying out the cyberattack gained access by impersonating staff rather than a systems or technical failure.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in July that his organisation had scrapped plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors following a widespread backlash.

The plan ‌involved raising up to $4.2bn by selling a 20 percent stake in a new unit that would run FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

articles.title: Aston Villa: Alejandro Garnacho already at a career crossroads at Villa Park
articles.summary: Alejandro Garnacho's brief Aston Villa career already looks over, so what next for the 22-year-old?
articles.body:
Alejandro Garnacho's time at Aston Villa has been brief - and it already looks to be over.

The latest snub by Villa boss Unai Emery was the most damming of all, with the on-loan Chelsea winger left out of Tuesday's Champions League defeat at Galatasaray.

"The players who were here I think are the best players to be here with us," said Emery.

Villa could have had 12 substitutes in Istanbul but Emery chose just 11 - including two goalkeepers - as Garnacho stayed at home.

The plan was for the Argentina international's loan move to become permanent for £43m should certain criteria be met.

They are believed to be based on a number of appearances staff felt were so achievable the club were in little doubt he would become a Villa player.

But now there is doubt he will ever play for them again.

"First start after three months. Happy to be enjoying football again."

The post Garnacho wrote on social media after a pre-season game in July has - along with anything else related to Villa - been deleted from his account.

He has played just 34 minutes in the Premier League this season, and seven of Villa's 11 games ended without him getting on the pitch.

His last appearance - just a three-minute cameo - came in the 1-1 draw against Fulham on 31 October.

Including Saturday's 0-0 draw with Sunderland , Garnacho has been omitted from the past three matchday squads - a strong sign Emery has lost faith in him.

But he may have been fighting a losing battle from the off, having arrived at Villa unfit.

Sources have acknowledged the 22-year-old was not at the level required and were surprised how off the pace he was when he signed in July.

He initially trained on his own, and questions over the signing were already being asked, with eyebrows raised by some internally given his inconsistent form for both Chelsea and Manchester United .

Yet he had been on Villa's list of targets - albeit a long list - while he was at Stamford Bridge as Emery was keen to sign a pacy winger in the summer.

Garnacho's problems were compounded by a head injury suffered in Thailand in pre-season, and even a boot camp during the international break in September and October, and scoring in friendlies against Sevilla and Southampton have not helped.

One of the issues Villa have is there is no exit clause, and both teams would have to agree to end the season-long loan deal early.

This time last year, Emery had already decided not to sign Harvey Elliott permanently in a £30m deal , leaving the on-loan Liverpool midfielder in limbo for the rest of the season.

And it appears Emery has already come to the same conclusion with Garnacho.

With Villa unable to find a solution with Liverpool , Elliott wasted a precious year of his career. Those close to him recognise the damage last season did, playing just nine times after being named Player of the Tournament at the European Under-21 Championship in 2025.

He is now at Valencia and is yet to start in La Liga this season.

The risk of going on loan to Villa became a topic of conversation in the game because of Elliott's plight, with sources suggesting players would think twice about joining the club. Garnacho's situation only increases those concerns.

Three times in two seasons, Emery and Villa have signed a high-profile player on loan only for it to fail.

Jadon Sancho's expensive loan from Manchester United last season - Villa paying a guaranteed 80% of Sancho's wages of more than £200,000 a week - ended with him having made just nine Premier League starts and scoring once in 39 appearances - 21 of those as a substitute.

Sancho may have played more than Elliott and Garnacho - and came off the bench in their Europa League win - but what value did Villa really get?

Of course, Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio enjoyed positive loan spells previously - Rashford returning to the England squad while at Villa - but they are exceptions to the rule.

Nicolo Zaniolo, Clement Lenglet and Axel Disasi have joined in recent years and barely merit footnotes, while Douglas Luiz's loan return last season did not prompt a return to the heights he had reached previously at Villa.

The club have constantly complained about financial restrictions with some justification, but questions can certainly be asked about the money spent on many of their signings.

The blunt truth is there is no clear path.

Teenager George Hemmings has just signed a new deal and has earned praise from Emery for understanding the way he wants his players to work.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson are also ahead of Garnacho, leaving him well behind even before regulars John McGinn, Johan Manzambi and Emi Buendia are factored in.

There was interest from abroad in the summer, with Roma keen, and it seems increasingly unlikely we will see Garnacho at another Premier League club soon.

Fifa rules allow players to play for two clubs in a season - or three if they move to a team whose season overlaps like the MLS - meaning Garancho could feature for another, unlike Elliott as he had already played for Liverpool and Villa.

Garnacho, whose character has not been called into question while at Villa, cost Chelsea £40m when he signed from Manchester United in 2025 but failed to make a consistent impression, with eight goals in 43 games. When he joined Chelsea he signed a contract until 2032.

Prior to that, United boss Ruben Amorim had told him to leave.

Now nothing, it seems, will persuade Emery that Garnacho is worth persevering with - leaving the winger's career continuing to drift.

articles.title: Ohio State vs Michigan: Buckeyes who had breakout games in The Game
articles.summary: Chris Olave had five catches all season before Michigan in 2018. Then came two touchdowns and a blocked punt. Here are other breakouts vs. Michigan.
articles.body:
They say careers are made in The Game between Ohio State and Michigan . It's not just a saying. Some of the greatest Buckeyes of all time announced themselves against Michigan -- players nobody was talking about on Friday who were legends by Saturday night.

Here are the best breakout performances by Ohio State players against the Wolverines throughout the history of one of -- if not the -- greatest rivalries in all of American sports.

The gold standard. Before the 2018 game, Olave was a three-star freshman with five catches for 70 yards all season. He wasn't in the receiver rotation until Austin Mack got hurt. Most Ohio State fans didn't know his name.

Then Michigan happened. Olave caught two passes for 48 yards -- both 24-yard touchdowns, the first two scores of his career. Then he blocked a punt that Sevyn Banks returned 33 yards for a touchdown. Ohio State won 62-39.

"It changed my career," Olave said later. "I believe it changed my career, having that game." As a sophomore, he led Ohio State in receiving yards (849) and touchdowns (12). The rest is history.

Same game, different breakout. Haskins was in his first season as Ohio State's starting quarterback, and he shredded Michigan's top-ranked defense: 20-of-31 for 396 yards, six touchdowns, no interceptions. The six touchdown passes shattered the single-game passing records for The Game.

Haskins went on to finish third in the Heisman voting that year. The Michigan game was the performance that made everyone take notice.

Smith was already the Heisman frontrunner coming into the Game of the Century. But the game against No. 2 Michigan was the one that sealed it: 29-of-41 for 316 yards and four touchdowns against one of the best defenses in the country, in a 42-39 win.

Smith won the Heisman a few weeks later. The Michigan game was his closing argument.

Samuel did a little of everything in the double-overtime classic -- 54 rushing yards, 32 receiving yards, and a swerving, change-of-direction run on the play before J.T. Barrett's famous fourth-down conversion. Then, on the very next play after "The Spot," Samuel took a handoff 15 yards into the end zone to win it 30-27.

Meyer calls the 2016 win the most unforgettable moment of his life outside of family. Samuel's run is the reason.

The 42-41 win in Ann Arbor was a track meet, and Miller and Hyde were the engines. Miller ran for 153 yards and three touchdowns and threw for 133 yards and two more scores -- five total touchdowns on just 286 yards of offense.

Hyde was even better on the ground: 27 carries for 226 yards and a touchdown. That's still the most rushing yards by an Ohio State player in a game against Michigan.

Wells carried the ball 39 times for 222 yards and two touchdowns in a 14-3 win in Ann Arbor -- in a game where neither team could throw the ball and everyone in the stadium knew what was coming.

Wells accounted for 222 of Ohio State's 279 total yards that day. Seventy-nine percent of the offense. One man. At the time, it was the most rushing yards by a Buckeye against Michigan. Hyde broke the record six years later.

The 56-27 rout in Ann Arbor was a two-man show. Dobbins carried 31 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns -- the first Buckeye in more than 50 years to run for four touchdowns against Michigan. Fields threw for 302 yards and four touchdowns, tying Troy Smith's record for the most passing touchdowns by an Ohio State quarterback in The Game.

That's the fun of this list. Every one of these players was either unknown or unproven before their Michigan moment. Olave had five catches. Haskins was in his first year as a starter. Samuel was a role player.

Saturday, someone will get their shot. Maybe it's Luke Fahey, the freshman quarterback in his first Game. Maybe it's a receiver not named Jeremiah Smith. Maybe it's a defensive player who makes the play that turns the game.

That's the thing about The Game. You never know whose career is about to change.

articles.title: Penn State vs. Maryland: Game Preview
articles.summary: The Nittany Lions attempt to end the regular season on a winning note following an all-time dud of a loss to Rutgers. Penn State (6-5, 3-5) vs. Maryland (4-7...
articles.body:
The Nittany Lions attempt to end the regular season on a winning note following an all-time dud of a loss to Rutgers.

Penn State (6-5, 3-5) vs. Maryland (4-7, 2-6)

Kickoff: 3:30 p.m., SECU Stadium, College Park, MD

The Betting Line: Penn State -7.5 (Fanduel)

TV: FS1, 3:30 p.m., Dan Hellie (play-by-play), Robert Smith (analyst)

Weather: A partially sunny and clear day with highs in the upper-50s.

MARYLAND RECORD: 2-2, 1st Year (Interim)

Chase Sowell has gained a first down on 80% of receptions this season, ranking second in FBS play…Tony Rojas was the first Penn State player to record 15 tackles and 2.5 TFLs in a game since Mike Hull in 2014 against Ohio State…the Nittany Lions have scored a rushing touchdown in 21 consecutive Big Ten games…Penn State is 44-3-1 all-time against Maryland and holds a 15-1 record on the road in the series.

The Terps offense is led by sophomore Malik Washington, a talented dual-threat quarterback who Maryland will build its offense around in 2027 – unless another program lures him away to do the same. He's completing 60.8 percent of attempts for 2,309 yards with 11 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. While those numbers may not jump off the page, Washington has regularly needed to force throws while playing from behind. He does have the arm talent to make big plays when the opportunity presents itself, and can also be dangerous as a runner.

Washington will look often to Chris Durr Jr., the most reliable part of the passing attack who already has 74 catches and will be looking to cross the 1,000 receiving yards threshold on Saturday. Receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding, Kaleb Webb and tight end Dorian Flemming are all imposing targets that can cause mismatches.

Maryland running back DeJuan Williams is similar to Rutgers' Antwan Raymond- a versatile back that can run between the tackles, but also create explosive runs and be a component in the passing game. Raymond had just under 150 yards from scrimmage and two scores to fuel the Scarlet Knights comeback. Penn State will need to find answers to slow down Williams to avoid another big day out of the backfield.

The big storyline for the Nittany Lions offense is the condition of the backfield. Leading rusher Carson Hansen was unable to play against Rutgers and his status for Saturday is unknown. Cam Wallace, who has hit his stride during the second half of the season, is also questionable and may be unavailable. James Peoples has already been ruled out after exiting the Rutgers game with an injury.

That could leave Penn State with just Quinton Martin Jr. as the only available experienced running back. Martin has mostly been forgotten about during conference play, and had just 12 yards on seven carries in relief duty against Rutgers – which comes out to 1.2 yards per carry, with his longest run of the day being 3 yards. However, Martin was able to shine when given the opportunity, including a 105-yard day against Clemson in the Pinstripe Bowl and a 100-yard day against Buffalo early this season.

This could be a troublesome development for a Penn State offense that attempts to run first to set up explosive plays in the air. If Hansen and Wallace are unavailable or limited, Rocco Becht may be forced to carry the offense. While Becht has had his moments as a Nittany Lion, he has been far from viewed as a difference-maker who has more starts than any other quarterback in the nation.

Becht will certainly be looking to Chase Sowell often, who has proven to be Penn State's most reliable option to create explosive plays. He has 399 receiving yards and three scores in the last three games alone, and is coming off a 123-yard day against the Scarlet Knights. Tight ends Benjamin Brahmer and Andrew Rappleyea will also be regular targets, especially if the short passing game is needed to replace rushing attempts. Wide receiver Brett Eskildsen is doubtful after an injury against Rutgers, which would led to more targets for Zay Robinson, an explosive option that has had more of a presence in the offense down the stretch.

Maryland's defense has been among the worst in the Big Ten this season. They are 16th in the scoring defense, allowing 30.7 points per game. The Terps rank 15th in rush defense and explosive plays allowed , and 13th in rush defense. However, it should be noted that Rutgers ranked worse in all categories, yet still held Penn State to just eight second-half points in their comeback victory over the Nittany Lions.

Keep an eye out for Terps linebacker Zion Elee, a five-star prospect with immense upside. The true freshman has just 10 tackles, but those include 6 TFLs and 3 sacks. He is primed to make a momenting-shifting play, which could come on at a key moment on Saturday.

Maryland kicker Sean O'Haire is 10-of-14 on field goals for the season, with a long of 46 yards. He has missed both attempts of 50+ yards this season. Punter Bryce McFerson is in his fourth-year as starter for the punts, but has a career-low 41.2 yards per punt, after averaging at least 44.2 yards in his first three seasons. He has several attempts of 60+ yards throughout his career.

How do you predict the outcome for a team like Penn State that has made inconsistency their identity after 11 games? Well, you throw your hands up in the air and hope they can't lose to a team like Maryland, despite all the injuries piling up and the Terps finding some late-season momentum. It worked for picking a victory over Purdue, so let's just stick with that logic. Either way, I'll enjoy my plate of leftover stuffing and pumpkin pie.

articles.title: Soule shines: 10 goal contributions in 17 matches
articles.summary: It wasn’t Hercules, but Matias Soulé who lit up the Parc des Princes. The Argentine talent took just five minutes to become the star of yet another great Eur...
articles.body:
It wasn't Hercules, but Matias Soulé who lit up the Parc des Princes.

The Argentine talent took just five minutes to become the star of yet another great European night: a decisive assist for Hermoso after dancing to the ball, skipping past opponents.

Gian Piero Gasperini expressed his satisfaction at seeing a player continually improving: "Besides being strong, he's very positive, he's receptive, and he wants to grow. He's 23, and he's in a period where he can grow, as he is doing. He's more complete than before; today he's played on the left, whereas until last year he was stuck on that pitch. He's reaching extraordinary technical and physical maturity. I'm happy for him; in these last two months, he's been doing something very positive."

Matias Soulé shows no signs of slowing down his unstoppable growth. The Argentine winger has already been involved in 10 goals this season, one every 114 minutes: four goals and six assists in 17 appearances.

The Argentine talent's performances this year are rising in proportion to the quality of his opponents: he has rarely been without a hand in big matches.

In fact, Soulé scored one goal and provided three assists in the Champions League matches against Real Madrid, Manchester United, and PSG.

In the league, he was instrumental with a goal that allowed Roma to a last-gasp 2-1 victory against Atalanta, adding to his assist for Hermoso that temporarily tied the game 1-1. On October 24, he lit up the Maradona stadium with a total performance from start to finish, further enhanced by the goal that sparked the comeback to secure a 3-3 draw at Napoli.

articles.title: Opponent watch: 24-year-old Alaves winger emerges as biggest threat for Real Madrid
articles.summary: Real Madrid will need to pay close attention to Angel Perez when Alaves visit the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday, November 28. This is because the 24-year-old...
articles.body:
Real Madrid will need to pay close attention to Angel Perez when Alaves visit the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday, November 28.

This is because the 24-year-old wing-back arrives after scoring and assisting in Alaves' 3-1 victory over Deportivo La Coruna, while his overall statistics identify him as one of La Liga's most productive attacking players.

Notably, Perez scored just 84 seconds into the match against Deportivo, which is now the second-fastest goal in La Liga this season.

He then supplied the cross for Lucas Boye's second-half goal, completing a performance that showed his ability to hurt opponents both by attacking space and creating for others.

The Deportivo performance was not an isolated contribution, as Perez has recorded five assists this season, with four in La Liga and one in the Copa del Rey.

As a result, he leads La Liga's full-backs and wing-backs for total assists and ranks second for assists per game.

Furthermore, Perez also leads the league in successful open-play crosses and shots on target per 90 minutes.

He also leads La Liga wing-backs for dribbles that lead to a shot per 90, while ranking third across Europe's top five leagues in that category.

Bernabeu presents a different kind of test

Perez's threat comes from the variety of ways he can contribute, as he can drive forward with the ball, beat a defender in the final third or deliver an accurate cross from wide areas.

Angel Perez was a menace for Deportivo. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Alaves' structure can also give him opportunities to advance from the right flank, which is why Real Madrid will need to manage the space behind their wide players and avoid allowing Perez to receive the ball facing forward.

If he is given time to pick out a delivery, Alaves can turn his attacking quality into a direct threat in the penalty area.

Perez's first goal against Deportivo showed exactly how he can exploit a defensive lapse. His assist for Boye then showed the danger that remains even after the initial attack has been contained.

Real Madrid therefore need to limit his forward runs, pressure him before he can deliver and ensure that his movement does not pull their defensive shape apart.
